source.attribution: Propane vapour pressure at 300 K: 9.974 bar, as cited in specs/models/eos/pure_saturation.toml
source.notes: The saturation pressure's attribution is inherited from eos.pure_saturation, whose spec case compares the Peng-Robinson value (9.9791 bar) against the published 9.974 bar. The published figure itself has not been checked against a primary source by a person, which is why this case is unverified - the flash's boundary is only as external as the number it is compared to. What IS independently established here is the direction: away from the boundary the sign of the fugacity difference is not in doubt.

derivation: A pure component cannot have a two-phase solution at all: with one component, the Rachford-Rice equation reduces to a single K-value, and a split needs K > 1 and K < 1 simultaneously. So the flash's answer for a pure feed is a phase diagnosis, and the diagnosis switches exactly where ln phi_L = ln phi_V - which is the definition of the saturation pressure. At 300 K that is 9.9791 bar from these kernels against a published 9.974 bar, +0.05%. This case takes 9.0 bar, about 10% below it, where the sign of ln phi_L - ln phi_V is unambiguous.
